t.1.41.1: O Rāma, when Sagara had gone the way of time, the people of the realm chose the most righteous Aṃśumant as their king.
t.1.41.2: O delight of the Raghus, that king Aṃśumān was exceedingly great. His son was the great Dilīpa, renowned by that name.
t.1.41.3: Having entrusted the kingdom to that Dilīpa, O Raghunandana, he performed exceedingly severe austerities on a delightful peak of the Himavat.
t.1.41.4: And for thirty-two thousand years the greatly renowned king, rich in austerities, having gone to the penance grove, attained heaven.
t.1.41.5: But the greatly radiant Dilīpa, having heard of the slaying of his grandfathers, could reach no decision, his mind being stricken with grief.
t.1.41.6: "How can Gaṅgā be brought down? How can the water rites for them be performed? And how might I deliver them?" Thus he became absorbed in anxious thought.
t.1.41.8: But the greatly radiant Dilīpa, having worshipped with many sacrifices, ruled the kingdom as king for thirty thousand years.
t.1.41.7: To him, ever brooding and known for his righteousness, a son named Bhagīratha was born, supremely devoted to dharma.
t.1.41.9: Without reaching any decision about their deliverance, the king, O tiger among men, was overcome by illness and met his death.
t.1.41.11: But Bhagīratha, the righteous royal sage of great splendour, O delight of the Raghus, was without offspring; though longing for progeny, he remained childless.
t.1.41.10: Having consecrated his son Bhagīratha in the delightful kingdom, the king, a bull among men, went to the world of Indra through the deeds he himself had earned.
t.1.41.12: O Raghunandana, he undertook a long austerity at Gokarṇa, standing with arms raised, practicing the penance of the five fires, eating only once a month, his senses subdued.
t.1.41.13: As he remained for thousands of years in fierce austerity, the blessed Brahmā, lord of creatures and sovereign master, became well pleased with him.
t.1.41.14: Then the Grandsire, approaching together with the hosts of gods, spoke to the great-souled Bhagīratha, who was practicing austerities.
t.1.41.15: O Bhagīratha, greatly fortunate one, O lord of men, I am pleased with you and with your well-performed austerity; choose a boon, O you of excellent vows.
t.1.41.16: The greatly illustrious and highly fortunate Bhagīratha, standing with joined palms, spoke to him, the grandsire of all the worlds.
t.1.41.18: When the ashes of these great-souled ones are drenched with the water of Gaṅgā, all my great-grandfathers would go to heaven forever.
t.1.41.17: If the Lord is pleased with me, and if my austerity bears any fruit, then may all the sons of Sagara obtain water from me.
t.1.41.20: To the king who had spoken these words, the Grandsire of all the worlds replied with an auspicious and sweet speech, sweet in its every syllable.
t.1.41.19: O god, let offspring be granted, and may our family not perish. In the family of the Ikṣvākus, O god, let this be my supreme boon.
t.1.41.21: Great is this desire of yours, O Bhagīratha, mighty chariot-warrior; so be it, may good fortune be yours, O enhancer of the Ikṣvāku lineage.
t.1.41.22: This Gaṅgā, daughter of Himavat, is his eldest daughter; to bear her, O king, let Hara be appointed to that task.
t.1.41.24: Having thus spoken to the king and having addressed Gaṅgā, the god, the creator of the worlds, went to heaven together with all the hosts of Maruts.
t.1.41.23: O king, the earth will not endure the fall of Gaṅgā. O hero, to sustain the two of them I see none other than the trident-bearer.
